elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: New 12(c): "TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold Client and its affiliates harmless from and against any third-party claim" — express defence duty running to Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 12(c) indemnity is expressly directed to "Client and its affiliates" and is scoped to "any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: 12(c)(i): "an allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services or the Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — the Agreement's service/deliverable items are named.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: 12(c)(iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data caused by TrueLink" — covers Client data generally, not merely a named subset.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of any claim under this Section 12".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement of such claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 12(a) as rendered is reduced to "(i) Client Content, and (ii) any violation by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the former breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default and product-liability limbs are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: 12(c)(i) provides a third-party IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity in favour of Client.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no modification exclusion was inserted, so nothing conflicts with the permitted (but not required) carve-out — condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion inserted, so the condition does not apply and the element is not violated.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion inserted, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered 12(c) or elsewhere in the cited language.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy is included in the inserted indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap language was added; the inserted indemnity is uncapped (which is more favourable to us, but the fallback element is literally unmet).

reasons: Preferred level is complete: inserted 12(c) supplies the express defence duty, affiliate coverage, third-party claim scope, IP infringement of the Interface/Hosting/Support Services, TrueLink's breach of applicable law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client data, and gross negligence/willful misconduct, plus notice, control-of-defence and reasonable-cooperation mechanics.

Customer-side narrowing is achieved in operative text: 12(a) now runs only to Client Content and Client's violation of applicable law, deleting the breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default and product-liability limbs — deletions required by the tenth preferred element, not cosmetic.

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund remedy, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is met; the drafter's reason for declining the fallback (avoiding a new cap on a currently uncapped indemnity) is coherent.

Minimality holds: existing favourable 12(b) TrueLink breach indemnity is retained untouched, the insertion tracks the model language without survival tails, at-own-expense wording, extra damages categories or unrelated boilerplate, and no requirement outside the checklist is added.

Minor observation only (not a minimality failure): the procedure sentence is drafted as applying to "any claim under this Section 12", so notice/control/cooperation also govern 12(a) and 12(b); this is mutual, standard, and required by the procedure elements — if the counterparty objects, it can be confined to Section 12(c).

Intent preserved: no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created (Client Content is an existing defined/used term carried over from the original 12(a)(iii)), and no retained sentence contradicts the new 12(c).
